answer.evidence: The main basin is an ellipse that runs from the back rim at row 46 to the front rim at about row 72. It has an elliptical rim ring and a teal water surface with ripples visible inside the opening (rows 48-69). Below it is a curved ashlar front rim face of about 8 rows (rows 72-79) with a dark outline at the bottom. The two tiered bowls on the central pillar also show elliptical mouths with water seen from above. The star finial and the water streams are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The fountain reads clearly, with an elliptical rim, ashlar blocks, ripple rings and a gold star finial. Its outline is a tinted dark grey-blue beside the stone and a dark teal beside the water, not a neutral black line. This matches the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels. The shading is shallower than the references. The stone has about 3-4 lightness steps (light, mid, dark, with sparse highlights) and the water has about 3-4 teal steps. The well and stall references carry about 5-6 per material, with per-stone and per-plank speckle. The candidate's measured 4 visible tones per full tile is far below the roofed well (20) and cheese stall (17), and below the hedge (9). Flat coverage of 8% is low but not zero, and the rim faces, the water inside the basin and the pillar bowls have smooth runs with little grain. That makes the piece look smoother and more simplified than the references. The tile density measurement may be partly pulled down by the flat-ish grass backdrop, but by eye the fountain is still thinner in texture than the well, so I fail it when in doubt.
